title: Needs some redesign to be competitive with similar products...
text:
Needs some redesign to be competitive with similar products.... First things first -- this is intended to be used on sparkling wine bottles: champagne, prosecco, cava, etc. It won’t work on still wine bottles because the neck and lip of the bottle are shaped differently from sparkling wine bottles. So bear that in mind if you're considering using this on your favorite chardonnay or Rioja -- it won’t fit.

So how does it work on bubbly bottles? I tried it on a bottle of prosecco and a bottle of brut sparkling wine (Korbel). No instructions were provided in the package but it wasn’t that difficult to figure out. The problem is that it doesn't work all that well. I have a couple of similar bottle sealers intended for use on champagne bottles so I’m familiar with the concept, but the problem is that this one just doesn’t seal all that well. The ”wing” -- that bit that wraps around the bottle below the lip -- isn’t all that sturdy. I’ve used this on only two bottles so far and I’m not sure it will last through another bottle. Plus, the seal isn’t really air tight.

For the same basic cost, you can get a similar stopper with double wings (each side of the bottle is ”gripped”), all constructed with metal.

Bottom line: thus needs some serious redesign to match or beat its competition. I’d start with the materials used in fabrication. Sorry -- I don’t like it. 2 stars.
